## I SCOPE AND INTERPRETATION

## Scope and interpretation of this Part

## 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] (a) Section 2 relates to applications for a writ of habeas corpus for release; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] (b) Section 3 relates to applications for a writ of habeas corpus to give evidence or a writ of habeas corpus to answer a charge.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] (The Family Procedure Rules 2010 1 contain rules about applications for a writ of habeas corpus for release in relation to a minor.)

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] (2) In Sections II and III—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] (a) “judge” means a judge of the High Court; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] (b) “court” means the High Court,

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.1 This Part contains rules about applications to the court as follows —] unless otherwise specified.

## II APPLICATIONS TO THE HIGH COURT FOR A WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS FOR RELEASE

## How to make the application for a writ of habeas corpus for release

## 87.2

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (1) The applicant must make the application by filing—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (a) a claim form under Part 8; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (b) a witness statement or affidavit.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (2) The witness statement or affidavit must—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (a) state that the application is made at the instance of the person being detained;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (b) set out the nature of the detention; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (c) subject to paragraph (3), be made by the detained person.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (3) If the detained person is unable to make the witness statement or affidavit, the witness statement or affidavit—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (a) may be made by some other person on behalf of the detained person; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (b) must state the reason why the detained person is unable to make the witness statement or affidavit.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (4) The claim form must be filed in the Administrative Court.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (5) The application may be made without notice.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (6) In cases of urgency, the judge—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (a) may dispense with the requirement that a claim form must be filed; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.2] (b) must give directions for the conduct of the application.

## Initial consideration of the application by a single judge

## 87.3

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.3] (1) A judge may consider an application under rule 87.2 initially on paper.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.3] (2) If an application has not been considered initially on paper, it must be considered—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.3] (a) by a judge sitting in court, unless rule 87.7 applies; or

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.3] (b) if no judge is sitting in court, by a judge otherwise than in court.

## Initial consideration of the application on paper

## 87.4

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (1) Where the judge considers the application under rule 87.2 on paper, the judge may—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (a) make an order for the issue of the writ;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (b) adjourn the application to a hearing;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (c) direct that the application be considered by a Divisional Court of the King’s Bench Division;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (d) direct that the application continues as an application for permission to apply for judicial review;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (e) give such other directions for resolution of the application as may be appropriate; or

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (f) dismiss the application.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (2) Where the judge dismisses a paper application, the applicant may request the decision to be reconsidered at a hearing.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (3) A request under paragraph (2) must be filed within 7 days after service of the order dismissing the application.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.4] (4) The applicant and the respondent must be given at least 2 days’ notice of the hearing date.

## Consideration of the application at a hearing

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] 87.5 Where the judge considers the application under rule 87.2 at a hearing, including a hearing ordered under rule 87.4(1)(b) or a hearing requested under rule 87.4(2), the judge may—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (a) make an order for the issue of the writ;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (b) adjourn the application to a further hearing;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (c) direct that the application be considered by a Divisional Court of the King’s Bench Division;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (d) direct that the application continues as an application for permission to apply for judicial review;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (e) give such other directions for resolution of the application as may be appropriate;

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (f) dismiss the application; or

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Consideration of the application at a hearing] (g) order that the detained person must be released.

## Order for release: sufficient authority to release detained person

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Order for release: sufficient authority to release detained person] 87.6 An order made under rule 87.5(g) is sufficient authorisation for a governor of a prison, police officer or other person to release the detained person.

## Applications involving protected parties

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > Applications involving protected parties] 87.7 Any application made on behalf of a protected party must initially be considered by a judge otherwise than in court.

## Form and directions as to the return to the writ

## 87.8

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.8] (1) A writ of habeas corpus for release must be in Practice Form No. 89.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.8] (2) A court or judge issuing a writ of habeas corpus for release must give directions as to the court or judge before whom, and the date on which, the writ is returnable.

## Service of the writ

## 87.9

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.9] (1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), the applicant must serve the writ of habeas corpus for release personally on the respondent.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.9] (2) If it is not practicable to serve the writ personally, or if the respondent is the governor of a prison or other public official, the applicant must serve the writ by leaving it with an employee or agent of the respondent at the place where the detained person is being held.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.9] (3) If there is more than one respondent named in the writ, the original writ must be served according to this rule on the first-named respondent, and copies must be served on the other respondents.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.9] (4) The court must notify all parties–

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.9] (a) of the court or judge before whom, and the date on which, the writ is to be returned to the court; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.9] (b) that in default of obedience, proceedings for committal of the party disobeying may be taken.

## Return to the writ

## 87.10

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.10] (1) The return to a writ of habeas corpus for release must—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.10] (a) be indorsed on or annexed to the writ; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.10] (b) state all the causes of the detention of the detained person.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.10] (2) The return may be amended, or another return substituted for it, by permission of the court or judge before whom the writ is returnable.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.10] (3) The return must be filed and served upon the applicant in accordance with the directions of the court issuing the writ.

## Procedure at hearing of the writ

## 87.11 At the hearing of the writ an application may be made—

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.11 At the hearing of the writ an application may be made—] (a) to discharge or remand the detained person; or

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.11 At the hearing of the writ an application may be made—] (b) to amend or quash the return.

## III WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS TO GIVE EVIDENCE OR TO ANSWER A CHARGE

## Writ of habeas corpus to give evidence or to answer a charge

## 87.12

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.12] (1) An application for a writ of habeas corpus to give evidence or a writ of habeas corpus to answer a charge must be made to a judge and be supported by a witness statement or affidavit.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.12] (2) A writ of habeas corpus to give evidence must be in Practice Form No. 91.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.12] (3) A writ of habeas corpus to answer a charge must be in Practice Form No. 92.

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.12] (4) An application for an order to bring up a prisoner otherwise than by writ of habeas corpus, to give evidence in any criminal or civil proceedings before any court, tribunal or judge, must be–

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.12] (a) made to a judge or, in the case of an application for an order under section 57 of the County Courts Act 1984 2 , a judge of the County Court; and

[PART 87 – APPLICATIONS FOR WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS > 87.12] (b) supported by a witness statement or affidavit.
